skill.name: npm-helper
skill.description: NPM and Node.js package management guidance for project setup, dependency troubleshooting, workspaces, audits, and publishing workflows.
skill.summary: Manage npm, Yarn, and pnpm projects with structured dependency and package configuration guidance.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown fences, placeholder URLs, or benign package manager configuration examples. I confirmed the recursive sudo chown guidance as risky because it changes ownership of user or system package directories. No prompt-injection or credential-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the sudo chown examples or require explicit user confirmation before any privileged ownership change. Prefer safer npm prefix guidance from official documentation.
Avoid command substitution in sudo examples. Use clearer manual steps that show the target user and directory before execution.

remediation.issue: Package execution examples need review warnings
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to inspect packages before using global installs, npx commands, audit fix --force, or publishing commands.

static_findings.snippet: - Use exact versions in production (`npm install --save-exact`)
- Use `npm ci` in CI/CD for faster, reliable installs
- Use `npx` instead of global installs when possible

content.value_statement: JavaScript dependency work often slows teams with version conflicts, lock file questions, and package manager differences. This skill guides npm, Yarn, pnpm, audits, workspaces, and publishing tasks.
actual_capabilities: Compares npm, Yarn, and pnpm commands for common dependency workflows.
Guides project initialization for JavaScript, TypeScript, and ESM projects.
Explains package.json fields, scripts, dependency types, and engine settings.
Provides workspace examples for npm, Yarn, and pnpm monorepos.
Supports troubleshooting for module errors, peer dependencies, cache issues, and publish preparation.
Describes npm audit, dependency updates, lock files, and security review habits.
limitations: It does not verify whether a package or maintainer is trustworthy.
It does not replace manual review before running package install or publish commands.
Examples may need changes for different shells, operating systems, or package manager versions.
Some troubleshooting guidance touches user home configuration and needs careful confirmation.

use_cases.title: Set up a Node.js project
use_cases.description: Create a package plan with scripts, dependencies, TypeScript settings, and lock file guidance.

use_cases.title: Repair dependency problems
use_cases.description: Diagnose peer dependency warnings, module resolution errors, outdated packages, and cache-related install failures.

use_cases.title: Prepare a package release
use_cases.description: Review package metadata, publish settings, audit steps, version updates, and dry-run checks before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Package Manager
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose npm, Yarn, or pnpm for a new Node.js project. Explain the tradeoffs and first setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Install Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my npm install error and suggest safe steps to fix dependency, cache, or peer dependency problems.

prompt_templates.title: Design Workspace Scripts
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan package manager workspaces for this repository. Suggest scripts for build, test, clean, and dependency installation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my package release process. Check metadata, scripts, lock files, audit steps, tags, and publish safety controls.

output_examples.input: I need a TypeScript package setup with tests and linting.
output_examples.output: A setup plan covering package metadata, TypeScript configuration, development dependencies, scripts, source folders, tests, and lock file practices.

output_examples.input: npm install fails with peer dependency warnings.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting sequence that identifies the conflicting packages, explains peer dependency rules, and recommends safer fixes before legacy overrides.

output_examples.input: I want to publish my first scoped package.
output_examples.output: A release checklist for package fields, access settings, versioning, dry-run review, audit checks, and publish commands.

best_practices: Review install and publish commands before allowing an agent to run them.
Commit lock files and use clean installs for repeatable builds.
Audit dependency changes and package scripts before upgrading or publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not run privileged package-manager fixes without understanding the target paths.
Do not use audit fix --force before reviewing breaking changes.
Do not publish packages without a dry run and metadata review.

faq.question: Can this skill choose between npm, Yarn, and pnpm?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares common workflows, performance tradeoffs, lock files, and workspace support.

faq.question: Can it fix dependency conflicts automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest troubleshooting steps, but users should review commands before execution.

faq.question: Does it support TypeScript projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes TypeScript setup, scripts, dependency categories, and build guidance.

faq.question: Can it help with monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers npm, Yarn, and pnpm workspace patterns for common monorepo tasks.

faq.question: Does it check package security?
faq.answer: It explains audit workflows and review practices, but it does not independently verify package trust.

faq.question: Is it safe to run every command it suggests?
faq.answer: No. Review commands that install packages, change home configuration, use sudo, or publish packages.
